Q: How to dismiss Windows Security "Smart Card" dialog during Selenium/Robot Framework automated tests? A:

I can suggest my old solution for similar case - create your own Credential Provider.

Create some flag (memory/kernel/resource object) that indicate your current situation

Inside of SetUsageScenario filter out cpus only to CPUS_CREDUI scenario.

Inside of SetSerialization filter out pcpcs->ulAuthenticationPackage only to

PIN_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_ID.

Inside of GetCredentialCount check the flag:

  • if the flag is active - set the arguments values to:
*pdwCount = 1;
*pdwDefault = 0;
*pbAutoLogonWithDefault = TRUE;
  • other way set them to:
*pdwCount = 0;
*pdwDefault = -1;
*pbAutoLogonWithDefault = FALSE;

If the flag was set your provider will be imminently called with GetSerialization and your provider can set a return value:

*pcpgsr = CPGSR_NO_CREDENTIAL_FINISHED;

I hope it will help you.

Q: Questioning the design of SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY() in SQL Server A:

For example, let's make a variable that keeps tracking for identity changes for each table, would that not be better?

That's quite easily accomplished with this code:

INSERT INTO dbo.tblGender VALUES ('Male')  -- Line A
DECLARE @GenderIdentity INT = SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY();

INSERT INTO dbo.tblPerson VALUES ('Ibrahim', 'Ib@gmail.com', 1, 27) -- Line B
DECLARE @PersonIdentity INT = SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY();

Question: why was it designed that way and not other way?

Well - what would be your expected behaviour, if you run both lines A and lines B, inserting a row in tblGender and another into tblPerson - what would you expect SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY() to return in this case??
